  "report_markdown": "## Overview
Costco Wholesale Corp. operates membership warehouses and e-commerce sites globally, offering low prices on a limited selection of nationally-branded and private-label products [10-K line 00134]. Its business model is built on high sales volumes and rapid inventory turnover through volume purchasing, efficient distribution, and reduced handling in no-frills, self-service warehouse facilities [10-K line 00134]. The company buys most merchandise directly from suppliers, routing it to cross-docking consolidation points or directly to warehouses, creating freight volume and handling efficiencies [10-K line 00135]. Costco operates with shorter hours than many other retailers, resulting in lower labor costs relative to sales volume [10-K line 00140].

## Market Positioning and Growth Outlook
Costco competes globally with global, national, and regional wholesalers and retailers, including supermarkets, supercenters, online retailers, gasoline stations, hard discounters, department and specialty stores, and operators selling a single category or narrow range of merchandise [10-K line 00190]. Notable competitors in the U.S. include Walmart, Target, Kroger, and Amazon, as well as other warehouse clubs such as Sam’s Club and BJ’s Wholesale Club [10-K line 00190]. The company's competitive advantage includes a strong brand identity, particularly its private-label Kirkland Signature products, which are perceived by members as high quality at lower prices than national brands [10-K line 00192]. Costco also leverages its membership format and loyalty to drive repeat visits and consistent fee revenue [10-K line 00167].

Key growth drivers include increased comparable sales, driven by shopping frequency and average ticket size, as well as the opening of new warehouses [10-K line 00451]. The company’s membership base has grown consistently, with paid members reaching 84,100 thousand at the end of 2026 [10-K line 00161]. Executive membership penetration, which represented 75.2% of worldwide net sales in 2026, is another growth lever [10-K line 00166]. Additionally, digitally-enabled sales, representing 11% of total net sales in 2026, have grown at a faster pace than traditional sales [10-K line 00153].

## Future Developments and Strategic Recommendations
Costco's future developments include continued expansion of e-commerce operations and business centers, which complement warehouse operations [10-K line 00153]. The company plans to open new warehouses, with 28 new warehouses opened in 2026 (including three relocations), adding 25 net new warehouses [10-K line 00415]. Costco is also expected to continue its focus on employee engagement and retention, with a high U.S. and Canada retention rate of approximately 94% in 2026 [10-K line 00181]. Strategic recommendations include maintaining pricing flexibility, leveraging private-label products for margin expansion, and continuing investments in digital platforms to support growth in digitally-enabled sales [10-K line 00399].

## Investment Recommendation
**Thesis**

Costco demonstrates strong financial performance and business quality, with consistent revenue growth, robust net income, and a solid return on equity. The company's membership model, private-label products, and operational efficiency underpin its competitive advantage and profitability. Key drivers include increased comparable sales, new warehouse openings, and digital sales expansion. Despite some cyclical exposure and competitive pressures, Costco’s low-margin model and stable fee revenue provide resilience. The company also shows strong cash flow generation and a manageable debt-to-equity ratio.

**Investment Recommendation**

Buy
